analysis.title: Derivatives Market Overview, October 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 0.93% in October to 7,580.07, while the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.65% and ended nearly 10% below its October high. The selloff was led by technology.
On October 30 the NDX fell 3.5%, its worst day since June. One-month NDX implied volatility rose more than four vol points and closed at the 85th percentile on a one-year lookback.
QQQ options volume rose 12% from September and surged 66% on October 30 versus the prior five-day average.

The NDX-SPX volatility spread widened to nearly 10 vol points, close to double its early-October level. Implied and realized volatility both rose faster for NDX than SPX, which NISA reads as NDX's greater sensitivity to the AI theme.
VIX rose 3.08 points in October to 19.42. S&P 500 30-day realized volatility was 10.79%, up 0.64 pts.

U.S. equity financing term structure inverted at the end of October as the front end priced the higher cost of financing long positions over year-end. The rest of the curve shifted lower and traded in line with two-year medians for the first time since May.

Year-end financing spreads fell below the levels of the prior two years after running above them for much of the summer. Asset manager net S&P 500 futures positioning fell 8.6% from its May high and U.S. levered equity ETF AUM fell 25% from its June peak.
Questions remain over IPOs slated for the rest of the year, since heavy issuance could weigh on dealer balance sheets and reduce financing appetite.
Treasury yields retraced much of their September rise, with the 2-year yield ending October 30 bps lower. The MOVE Index fell 10.25 points to 100.20.

USD swaption skew repriced in short-dated expiries on short tails, where receivers traded at a premium to payers. The 3Mx1Y and 3Mx2Y 25-bp risk reversals both turned negative, while the 3Mx5Y stayed near zero. NISA reads this as demand tied to the near-term policy path, not to long-term rates.

China A-share index financing shows a persistent dislocation. A one-year total return swap on the CSI 500 trades at SOFR minus 1086 bps, so a long investor collects roughly 6.75%. The cause is one-way hedging flow from onshore market-neutral funds selling index futures, combined with limited foreign access and difficult short selling.

sector_views.rationale: The report describes technology as leading the October equity selloff and NDX volatility rising faster than SPX, but it gives no rating or directional recommendation.
